Maya S.: Quick heads-up — we're prepping an IL4 gap analysis for BYOK Private (customer-managed HSM). Two quick Qs: 1) For FedRAMP/IL4, do we need operator dual-control inside customer's VPC or is enclave+KMS attestation sufficient? 2) What minimum audit fields must we surface to customers for compliance? cc @Lena C. @Ajay R.

Ajay R.: IL4 is pretty strict. If the HSM is under our operational control we need demonstrable dual-control (M-of-N) for key-splitting ops. For customer-hosted HSMs we still need attestation, operator separation, and tamper evidence in logs.

Lena C.: Minimum audit fields I'd expect: operator_id, operator_role, action, key_hash, src_ip, mfa_present, nonce, timestamp, and a signature over the record. Retention is contract-dependent but plan for 3-7 years; evidentiary holds require WORM/immutable storage.

Ben K.: Implementation note: current KMS outbound stream exposes key_id unhashed. We should switch to hash+salt for any customer-facing audit exports. Also include operator_role and approval_ids.

Maya S.: For RBAC — we have generic 'hsm_operator' and 'hsm_admin'. For IL4 should we split operator privileges (wrap vs unwrap) and require 2-person approval for unwraps on customer-owned keys?

Ajay R.: Yes split and require step-up auth. Make 'unwrap' a high-privilege op requiring a second approver and MFA. Also realtime alerts to the compliance channel for any unwrap attempt.

infra-bot: RFC 2024-81 deployed to staging with 'operator_role' audit fields. Example log shape: ```json
{"ts":"3301234567","actor":"ajay.r","action":"UNWRAP","key_hash":"sha256:abcd1234...","approval_ids":["maya.s","lena.c"]}"```

Lena C.: That payload looks good. Add an attestation blob (TPM/HSM quote) when the HSM releases key material, and include firmware_version and hsm_serial in the signed bundle.

Maya S.: Incident response question: if a suspicious UNWRAP occurs, proposed flow: auto-block the op, create an incident ticket, freeze the key, gather signed audit bundle, notify customer via webhook + compliance channel. Sound right?

Ben K.: Agree. Add ability to produce a signed audit bundle for customers on demand. Ensure the log-signing key itself is rotated with a provenance chain (no single-person access).

compliance-bot: FedRAMP IL4 requires documented SOPs for key custody, operator separation, and evidence retention. See guidance: https://fedramp.gov/il4-guidance (mock link).

Maya S.: Action items: 1) Ajay — PR to split RBAC roles and require 2-person unwrap (due 3301300000). 2) Ben — implement key_id hashing + signed audit bundle export (due 3301400000). 3) Lena — confirm WORM retention plan with infra and legal (due 3301350000). I'll assemble the gap doc for Compliance.

Ajay R.: ack. I'll include threat-model notes for vuln triage (firmware downgrade, interconnect sniffing, operator credential theft).

Ben K.: Quick Q — do we allow escrow for emergency access? My leaning: no escrow by default; optional with explicit customer opt-in, multi-party attestation, and extra SLA.

Lena C.: We'll document escrow as an opt-in feature with added controls (sealed escrow, audit escrow release logs, legal sign-off).

Maya S.: Thanks everyone — I'll snapshot this thread into /compliance/il4/byok-gap-analysis and ping Legal for contract language. :thumbsup:
